svg.title: An actual spectral stack with prefix and test preservation
svg.desc: The finite Jones density gives a right-coordinate projection. A coordinate trace scales by n; the old algebra scales by n squared. A fixed prefix and an approximately preserved common basis retain the physical tests. Small joint defect remains a separate input.
svg.text: One realized projection; both canonical traces
Same physical inclusion N ⊂ M. Proofs: FC.3–FC.24 and V8.1–V8.33.
Finite Jones columns
h = Σ aᵢ e aᵢ*, Σ aᵢ aᵢ* = 1
ψₕ|M = τ; ψₕ E_A = ψₕ
q = supp(h), 1 ≤ Tr(q) ≤ L
L is finite for this density.
Actual matrix complement
D ≅ Mₙ ⊂ Tₖ ⊂ S ∩ Nₖ
New core: S⁰ = D′∩S ⊂ R⁰ = D′∩R
Ã = A⁰ ⊗ B(L²(D))
rⱼ = right(Eⱼⱼ), Σ rⱼ = 1
rⱼ commutes with old B and M.
The projection and traces
P = Σ pₜⱼ rⱼ ∈ Ã, P² = P
Tr̃(T rⱼ) = n Tr(T)
Tr̃(T) = n² Tr(T) for old T
Both center measures are retained.
Mesh and one simultaneous shift
H = (1/n)Σ pₜⱼ, η = Tr(q)/n < 1
‖H − h‖₁ ≤ η; Tr̃(P) = n² Tr(H)
joint(P)/Tr̃(P) ≤ (Jₕ + 2η)/(1 − η)
One θ: Σᵤ ‖[u,P]‖₂²/Tr̃(P) ≤ 2Σᵤ √εᵤ/(1 − η)
εᵤ = ‖u h u* − h‖₁; choose n after this L.
Prefix retention and later physical tests
F = Nₖ′∩M; the absorption map fixes F pointwise.
Fixed marked cups recover the entire old prefix.
It need not fix Nₖ pointwise by the tensor map.
Two deletions: ‖bᵢ⁰⁰ − bᵢ‖₂,τ < 4δ.
New test defect ≤ old defect + 4√(4δ² + χd).
Four right-coordinate cuts (scalar sample)
Eigenvalues: 1/4 and 3/4; n = 4, θ = 1/2.
Ranks of the four cuts: 2, 1, 1, 0.
Their average H equals h in this example.
The charged band and the remaining input
Lost relative trace r gives χ ≤ 2η/(1 − η) + 2r.
The positive band is [a, n²L]; further deletion
scales dimensions by b² and retains the prefix.
A larger matrix does not erase a positive Jₕ.
General joint balance and the full partition remain open.
Boxes and areas are schematic. The scalar sample is not an asserted ordinary Jones core.
Both rows use their inherited full-corner traces; the smaller and larger centers remain distinct.
Human context: S. Popa, Classification of amenable subfactors of type II (1994), §§4.2 and4.4.
Independent exposition and reproducible figure: GPT-6.1 Sol (OpenAI), October 2026; CC0 1.0.
